title: NJ EMT medication and expanded-scope table
body:
Three documents decide what a New Jersey EMT may give. Doses below are quoted from the protocols; nothing here is inferred.

- **N.J.A.C. 8:40A-10.1(b)** — the baseline scope of practice rule. https://www.nj.gov/health/ems/documents/reg-enforcement/njac840ar.pdf
- **Certificate of Waiver for EMT Scope of Practice, June 24, 2024**, NJ DOH OEMS — adds four expanded-scope items per approved agency. Application instructions: https://www.nj.gov/health/ems/documents/Expanded_Scope_Application_Instructions.pdf
- **NJ EMS Clinical Practice Protocols and Guidelines v1, effective 8/21/2025** — supplies the doses. https://www.nj.gov/health/ems/documents/NEWJERSEYEMSCLINICALPRACTICEPROTOCOLS_GUIDELINES_FINAL8.21.2025v1.pdf

## The baseline rule

`N.J.A.C. 8:40A-10.1(b)` authorizes oxygen administration, and at item `13` authorizes **assisting a patient to administer drugs previously prescribed for that patient**, limited to:

1. Prescribed metered dose inhaler
2. Sublingual nitroglycerin
3. Epinephrine auto-injector

That is the whole drug list in the regulation. Everything else an EMT gives comes from the statewide protocols and agency standing orders.

## The table

| Drug | Indication as published | Dose / route | Limits and contraindications | Protocol |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Oxygen | Hypoxia, dyspnea, shock, altered mental status | Titrate to `SpO2` at or above `94%`; `90%` accepted in COPD; `94-99%` in stroke | In ACS, give **only** for dyspnea, `SpO2` under `94%`, or heart failure signs | 1.0, 3.0, 2.23 |
| Aspirin | Suspected acute coronary syndrome, adult | `324 mg` PO chewable; if the patient already took `81 mg`, give the remaining `243 mg` | The protocol warns not to treat every chest pain automatically with aspirin and nitrates; judge likelihood of ACS first | 3.0 |
| Nitroglycerin (patient's own) | Persistent ACS symptoms, adult | Facilitate the patient's own SL nitroglycerin every `3-5 min` | Only while systolic BP stays at or above `100 mmHg`; total of `3` doses | 3.0 |
| Epinephrine auto-injector, adult | Anaphylaxis | `0.3 mg IM`, anterolateral thigh preferred | Repeat dosing requires medical command; do not delay transport | 2.2 |
| Epinephrine auto-injector, pediatric | Anaphylaxis | Age and weight appropriate `0.15 mg` auto-injector IM, anterolateral thigh preferred | Patients who receive epinephrine should be transported | 2.2P |
| Naloxone, adult | Suspected opioid overdose with severely depressed mentation and respiratory effort | Nasal spray `4 mg` into one nostril, **or** `1 mg (1 mL)` per nostril by atomizer to a maximum of `4 mg`; may repeat the initial dose after `5 min` | Ventilate with BVM and `100%` oxygen plus an NPA **first**; transport to the ED afterward | 2.3A |
| Naloxone, pediatric | Suspected opioid overdose | `4 mg` formulation: over `11 years` and/or over `40 kg`, `4 mg`, may repeat once every `3-5 min`. `2 mg` formulation: over `5 years` and/or over `20 kg`, `1 mg` per nostril for a total of `2 mg`, may repeat once | Same ventilate-first and transport rules | 2.3P |
| Oral glucose, adult | Hypoglycemia, glucose under `60 mg/dL` and/or symptoms | `1-2` tubes of commercially prepared glucose gel | Patient must be alert enough to swallow and protect the airway | 2.8A |
| Oral glucose, pediatric | Hypoglycemia | `0.5 g/kg` of commercially prepared glucose gel | Same alertness requirement | 2.8P |
| Albuterol | Wheezing consistent with asthma or COPD | `2.5 mg` via nebulizer, may repeat every `5 min`, **maximum 3 doses**; or assist the patient's own MDI at the prescribed number of puffs, repeatable every `5 min` to `3` doses | **Agency must be approved by the medical director and OEMS.** Additional dosing requires medical command. If rales suggest pulmonary edema, go to the CHF protocol instead | 2.5 |

> **Trap:** The MDI you assist with must contain albuterol, levalbuterol, an albuterol/ipratropium combination, or another bronchodilator rescue inhaler. It is not a license to assist with any inhaler in the house.

## The June 24, 2024 expanded scope waiver

The waiver granted relief from `N.J.A.C. 8:40-7.1(b)6 and 13i` and `N.J.A.C. 8:40A-10.1(b)6 and 13i`, because the code still points at the 1990s National Standard Curriculum that NHTSA replaced in 2009 with the National EMS Education Standards. It permits an approved BLS ambulance service to add:

1. **Albuterol sulfate** by metered dose inhaler or nebulizer, for patients experiencing wheezing
2. **CPAP** for patients with shortness of breath secondary to pulmonary edema
3. **PEEP valves** for all patients requiring bag valve mask ventilation
4. **Glucometers** for patients with altered mental status, including lethargy or unconsciousness, that may be consistent with a diabetic emergency

Approval is **per agency, not per EMT**. The service emails a complete application to ems@doh.nj.gov containing a cover letter from the owner, chief or CEO and the medical director; an education program with curriculum, lesson plan, cognitive examination and competency assessment instrument for each item; a written clinical protocol for each item; and written policies covering ALS request, storage and maintenance, sufficient quantities, competency assessment, quality assurance and improvement, documentation, equipment testing, and a CLIA waiver. Incomplete applications are not reviewed.

> **Key:** Naloxone and aspirin appear under the EMT heading in the 2025 protocols but are not written into the `8:40A-10.1(b)` list. Treat the protocol plus your agency's standing orders as the operative authority and confirm locally which of the four waiver items your service carries.

## What is not EMT scope in New Jersey

Vascular access, any drawn-up or IV drug including dextrose, diphenhydramine, methylprednisolone and ipratropium, intubation, needle thoracostomy, cardiac monitoring and 12-lead acquisition, and sedation all appear only under PARAMEDIC & MICN headings. On-line medical command **may not** authorize a procedure outside your defined scope.
